model_annotation: The image presents two bar charts, one for Deutschland (Germany) and one for the EU, illustrating the percentage of various metals (Aluminium, Kupfer, and Nickel) across three years: 2021, 2022, and 2023. The charts share a common structure, with the horizontal axis listing the metals and the vertical axis representing the percentage, ranging from 0 to 30% in increments of 5. Each metal is associated with three bars, colored blue (2021), purple (2022), and grey (2023), respectively. In the Deutschland chart, the Nickel bars are the tallest, with values of 25.1% in 2021 and 24.7% in 2022, while Aluminium has the shortest bars, with values of 3.6% in 2021, 2.7% in 2022, and 1.0% in 2023. The EU chart displays a similar pattern, with Nickel having the highest values (24.3% in 2021 and 23.3% in 2022) and Aluminium having relatively low values (3.2% in 2021, 2.8% in 2022, and 1.7% in 2023). The charts provide a clear visual representation of the changes in metal percentages over the three-year period for both Deutschland and the EU.
